avoid-backticks-in-bd-remember: Never put backticks in a bd remember / bd note argument written inline in a bash double-quoted string: bash runs the backtick content as command substitution BEFORE bd sees it, so the memory is stored mangled and the substituted command actually executes (on angr-9ke6b.59 a memory citing "cargo clippy --all-targets" inside backticks silently kicked off a real clippy build and dropped the text). Symptom: shell prints "use: command not found" or similar, and bd recall shows the backticked span missing. Fix: pass the text through a quoted heredoc first -- read -r -d '' MEM <<'EOF' ... EOF then bd remember "$MEM" --key ... -- and prefer plain double quotes over backticks for code tokens inside memory prose. Same hazard applies to $(...) and bare $VAR in memory text.
avoid-bd-recall-outside-repo-cwd: bd subcommands resolve the .beads/ database by walking up from the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY, and 'bd recall <key>' outside the repo tree exits 0 with EMPTY stdout instead of erroring. A scripted citation-repair pass (read body -> string-substitute -> 'bd remember --key') run from /tmp therefore silently reports 'no change' for every key and repairs nothing, with a zero exit status the caller trusts. Always pass cwd=<repo root> to subprocess.run (or cd first), and make the script assert the recalled body is non-empty before deciding it needs no edit. Hit while sweeping citations for the arch/mod_tests.rs split (angr-6cp06.76); the same shape bites any bulk edit driven by 'bd recall'. See [[bd-memory-citation-repair-pattern]] and [[refactor-memory-sweep-rule]].
avoid-cadet-phase3-sticky-eager-retry:
angr-ckdy (CADET solve.py phase-3 step-loop egg hunt): the 'while True: sm.step(); break if any active.addr==0x804833E' idiom CANNOT be made to converge under the Rust engine by a manager-level sticky-eager retry (option b in the bead). Two independent blockers, both proven iter69:
(1) OBSERVABILITY: the Rust VEX interpreter CHAINS basic blocks within one step(n=1), so a state executes THROUGH 0x804833E mid-step and never stops with pc==0x804833E. explore(find=0x804833E) works only because angr-027h (commit ed600427b) breaks the block chain AT find/avoid addrs; a bare step-loop sets no find addr, so the egg block is never observable as an active addr. Python angr is block-granular so its phase-3 works.
(2) EXPLOSION/CRASH: flipping to eager mode (set_use_deferred_forks(false)) on active_empty does re-seed and progress (active 1->27 by step 38), BUT without a find-target to STOP at, eager BFS keeps forking — active jumps 49->310 around step ~120 and SEGFAULTS via C-stack overflow in claripy _ast_serialize/_calc_hash (recursive AST hash on giant trees), through rust_callback_dispatch._handle_symbolic_branch_callback_inner. explore() masks this by stopping at find (step 38, active~27).
Conclusion: a real phase-3 fix needs BLOCK-GRANULAR stepping (stop the chain at every basic-block boundary when no explore is active) so the egg is observable AND the loop breaks before explosion. That is a large engine change, not the eager retry. iter69 shipped only the diagnostic counter deferred_forks_dropped() (RustExplorationManager::deferred_forks_dropped, bumped in core_outcome.rs::handle_core_outcome's UnconstrainedJump deferred-drop arm, and since angr-6cp06.20 also in stepping_bounce.rs::handle_unmodeled_call's resolve_function-error arm, which likewise has nowhere to put the forks). The Python _maybe_step_eager_retry was implemented then REVERTED because it turns a benign infinite-spin into a crash.
avoid-claripy-not-on-bv-guard: claripy.Not(ast) on a 1-bit BV AST returns the NotImplemented singleton instead of raising — it does NOT negate. The Rust engine's assumed-constraint log stores (guard: RustBV(1-bit), is_true) pairs; rustbv_to_claripy lowers a comparison-derived guard to a claripy Bool (Not works) but an Extract/Ite-derived guard to a 1-bit BV (Not silently yields NotImplemented, which used to get pushed into the exported constraint list). Always go through claripy_bridge::export::assumed_guard_to_claripy, which checks 'length is None' to distinguish Bool from BV and compares a BV guard against BVV(1|0, 1). Consumers: RustExplorationManager::_export_state_constraints (state_api.rs) and PythonCallbacks::call_inspect_constraints (callbacks/inspect.rs). GENERALIZATION (angr-fs8kb.81): the same sentinel can come back from ANY binary dunder rustbv_to_claripy_memo's BVOp dispatch calls, so every such call site in claripy_bridge/export.rs must run the shared reject_non_ast closure (None or NotImplementedType -> PyRuntimeError naming both operands) before returning the result — bitwise_dunder (And/Or/Xor) and compare_dunder (Eq/Ne) both do; a new dunder helper that skips it re-opens the hole. ORDERING: in compare_dunder the guard must run BEFORE the extract::<bool> unwrap, because that extract is truthiness-shaped (the file notes it accepts PyInt as well as PyBool) — guard-after would turn a None return into a plausible BoolV(False), i.e. a wrong answer rather than a bogus object. TEST RIG for this whole family: register a Python stand-in carrying 'op' and 'length' attributes in the identity cache (cache::store_claripy_ast_with_info) under a RustBV::Symbolic leaf's id; ensure_claripy_ast's SILENT(cat-c) fallback passes anything with an 'op' attr through untouched, so the stand-in reaches the BVOp dispatch as args[0] and its dunders are what gets called. See export_tests::compare_dunder_rejects_not_implemented_and_none; evict_claripy_ast(id) afterwards, the registry is process-global.
avoid-claripy-z3-ctx-in-cargo-tests: cargo-test binary CAN import claripy/z3 when PYTHONPATH points at the venv, but claripy-Z3_ast paths still cannot be tested in-crate: they need engine::install_python_z3_context (adopting Python's Z3_context as the Rust thread-local), a Z3_context is NOT thread-safe, and libtest runs tests on parallel threads -- two adopters concurrently SIGSEGV the whole binary. Even pinned to --test-threads=1 the SymContext::unsat_core_assumed verdict for constraints added via RustSolverContext::add_constraint_ast came out order-dependent (empty vs non-empty core for identical fixed code, depending on which tests ran earlier in the process). Cover claripy-AST solver paths in tests/engines/rust/test_solver_ops.py instead; keep cargo tests on the Python-free handle API (create_concrete/op_*/eval_handle) and on Z3AstPtr borrowed from Rust-built z3 nodes. Established in angr-sqfj8.125.
avoid-deferred-fork-base-mismatch:
Deferred fork base mismatch (step-driver family): MaxBlocks/BlockEnd path forks from successors[0] (carries accumulated taken-path constraints from prior forks in same block) - SimProc-native success path forks from a saved fork_base = successors[0].fork() taken BEFORE any constraints. process_deferred_forks_into (exploration/stepping_forks.rs since angr-5mnx3.71; formerly stepping.rs) matches MaxBlocks/BlockEnd's behavior. The MaxBlocks/BlockEnd semantics is correct (deferred forks share a common prefix of prior taken-path constraints, since they all happened during the same VEX block). Anchors: RustExplorationManager::apply_core_outcome (exploration/stepping.rs) for the MaxBlocks/BlockEnd arm vs the SimProc-native arm in core_outcome_handlers.rs. SECOND FORM (angr-6cp06.19): a Python-bouncing arm that passes pre_callback_snapshot: None. bounce() forwards deferred_forks into PendingBounce regardless of BounceKind, and _resume_after_simprocedure's fallback base state.fork() runs AFTER the callback's writes+constraints - so ANY dispatch_bounce arm (stepping_bounce.rs) that can carry forks must call exploration::helpers::pre_callback_snapshot_for. That helper is now the single decision point; treat a new arm that hardcodes None as guilty. PythonVEXFallback was the third arm found doing it. RESOLVED (angr-6cp06.24, characterized not changed): the SimProc-native success path does hand the POST-call state to process_deferred_forks_into_core, but for the shape the interpreter actually emits it does not matter -- interpreter/statements.rs's GuardClass::Symbolic arm inserts a BranchSnapshot next to EVERY stored_conditions entry, and build_unexplored_fork's snapshot arm (fork_from_snapshot) replaces registers+solver wholesale, so the sibling keeps the pre-branch, pre-call register file (no return-value write, no popped-return-addr SP bump). Only memory is inherited from the post-call base, and only when the snapshot's own memory is None. Pinned by exploration/core_outcome_tests/simproc_forks.rs. SECOND FINDING from the same work: the snapshot-LESS + stored-condition shape used to be UNSAT by construction in EVERY caller of process_deferred_forks_into_core -- add_fork_guard_constraint assumed the taken guard onto base BEFORE build_unexplored_fork's non-snapshot arm forked it onto the opposite guard, so the sibling was minted, pruned, and silently lost. Fixed in angr-z3obp: fork_unexplored_and_guard_base now owns the order (fork first, guard second); pinned by simproc_forks.rs::simproc_success_fork_without_snapshot_survives_with_opposite_guard. Still unreachable from the interpreter, but it is the trap any future unification of the two fork bases must avoid.

UPDATE (angr-6cp06.25, a REAL bug the .24 characterization missed): "the snapshot replaces registers+solver wholesale" only covers registers, memory and solver. Every OTHER per-state field -- RustSimState::fork_with copies them verbatim from the fork base -- is unprotected, and BranchSnapshot has no slot for them. native_resume_stack was the live instance: handle_native_resume_core pops the resume frame before materializing, so a sibling of a branch taken inside the guest sub-call body lost the frame and got deadended by the "empty resume stack" arm on reaching the sentinel; handle_simprocedure_core's NativeProcDisposition::SubCall arm pushes one first, so a sibling of a pre-call branch inherited a continuation it never entered. Fix: resume_stack_for_forks (capture BEFORE the mutation) + process_deferred_forks_rewound (swap just that field around process_deferred_forks_into_core) + RustSimState::replace_native_resume_stack; pinned by core_outcome_tests/native_resume.rs. syscall_continue needs no rewind (the syscall path never touches the resume stack). INVARIANT for future work: any handler that mutates a non-register, non-memory, non-solver state field before calling process_deferred_forks_into_core must rewind that field for the fork base, or move the mutation after materialization -- the snapshot cannot save you. Candidates to re-audit if they ever gain a pre-fork mutation: call_stack, fs, heap_brk/posix_brk/mmap_base, heap_metadata, getopt_*, stdin_symbols.
avoid-deny-on-mod-rs-parent: deny-sweep must NOT add module-level #![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)] to exploration/mod.rs: mod.rs declares every sibling submodule (scheduler, selection_policy, helpers, step_core, ...) via 'mod x;', and an inner-attribute deny propagates hierarchically into all those child modules — many carry dozens of un-allowed unwrap/expect and the build would break. Deny only the LEAF py-boundary body files individually (manager_methods/pending_api/state_api/stats_api/event/state_id/state_lifecycle/resume/run_loop). Same reason mirror-applies to any parent 'mod.rs' anywhere in the tree. COROLLARY (angr-c7xno.48): the same hierarchical propagation reaches a file's own #[cfg(test)] child and overrides lib.rs's crate-wide #![cfg_attr(test, allow(unwrap_used, expect_used))]. So any file at or under a denying module must declare its test sibling with the test_submod! macro (defined in lib.rs, textual scope, no import needed), never a hand-written '#[cfg(test)] #[path="x_tests.rs"] mod x;' — the macro's whole job is attaching the re-allow. The hand-written form compiles fine while the test file happens to contain no unwrap/expect, so it fails only for the next contributor.
avoid-dispatch-next-drain-loop-in-tests:
Unit tests that call exploration::scheduler::worker::dispatch_next MUST NOT drain with `while let Some(..)`. dispatch_next only returns None at quiescence (injector empty AND WorkTransport.pending == 0) or on cancel; a real worker retires each task with pending -= 1 after processing, so a test that absorbs children via absorb_continues (which counts them IN) and never decrements pending will hang FOREVER inside steal_from_injector's backoff sleep loop — a silent deadlock that looks like a slow `cargo test --release` (test binary alive, load average ~0). Dispatch a fixed count instead, or pre-set pending. Symptom-to-diagnosis: if cargo test --release runs >10min with near-zero CPU, pgrep the target/release/deps/rustylib-* binary — it is blocked, not compiling.

COROLLARY (angr-9ke6b.58, iter124): the same 'pending must be retired or the pool hangs' rule is what makes dispatch_next's reattach-failure arm correct — its pending.fetch_sub(1) is not just accounting hygiene, it is the ONLY thing that lets the following steal_from_injector see pending==0 and report quiescence. Any future worker-side path that DROPS a stolen payload must fetch_sub too. Both directions are now pinned by test_dispatch_next_corrupt_only_payload_reaches_quiescence (sole corrupt task -> None, pending 0) and test_dispatch_next_drops_a_corrupt_payload_and_keeps_stealing (corrupt ahead of a good payload; neither injector_dispatches nor reattaches counts the dropped steal — since angr-6cp06.21 both count only successful reattaches, keeping SchedulerStats::dispatches() equal to the states actually processed), both driving StateMigrationPayload::corrupt_for_test() and relying on Injector::steal being FIFO so the corrupt payload is stolen first.
avoid-enumerating-expect-sites-in-module: Panic-policy module-doc headers must NOT enumerate surviving expect/unwrap sites ('the one surviving expect is in X'). The #![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)] inner attribute propagates to ALL descendant modules, so a mod.rs header's count silently undercounts every #[allow] added in a sibling/child file — and nothing gates it. Confirmed stale three times: memory/mod.rs (angr-sqfj8.72) claimed 'one surviving expect pair in SymbolicMemory::merge' while memory/multi.rs held 2 more allow sites = 5 expects / 3 sites; procedures/mod.rs (angr-sqfj8.147) claimed 'the one surviving expect in symbol_counter' while ctype.rs (x2), fgets.rs and scanf.rs each carried one; exploration/scheduler_worker.rs (angr-c7xno.37) said 'the two .expect sites here are both job.results.lock() poison guards' with three sites, one of them a #[cfg(test)]-gated guard on a DIFFERENT mutex (job.summaries). All now state the INVARIANT instead: every surviving expect sits under a reviewed #[allow(clippy::expect_used, reason = "...")] naming the local guard that proves it, and that guard is never guest input; if you cannot write that reason the code needs an Error return, not an expect. Second, subtler drift found by the .147 sweep: a #[cfg(test)] child (inline mod tests, or a #[path]-included _tests.rs) opting out of the deny wholesale also makes a naive grep of the deny scope contradict an accurate header — say 'the one surviving NON-TEST expect' and name where the test opt-out lives (done in symbolic/context.rs, exploration/shadow_probe.rs, symbolic/solver_build.rs, symbolic/query_class.rs). Third, from .37: the fn-level #[allow]'s reason string drifts the same way — worker_loop's named only job.results while the fn also held a job.summaries guard — so audit the reason text, not just the module doc. Single-file boundary modules with no child mods at all may still enumerate; .147 verified stash.rs, state/snapshot.rs, state/filesystem/symbolic.rs, exploration/native_technique.rs, automaton/subset_construction.rs and symbolic/value_z3.rs accurate and left them. Companion to deny-sweep-function-level-allow-pattern (which governs allow granularity, not the doc).
avoid-fxhash-dedup-set-spike: Evaluated+REJECTED the last std-hash hot-path FxHash candidate for the autonomous loop: symbolic/local_constraints.rs LocalConstraints.dedup_set (HashSet<usize> of Z3 AST ptrs, seeded in constraint_ops.rs seed_and_check_z3_dedup, consulted per add_constraint_raw). NOT a measured-win spike because: (1) the only seed trigger add_constraint_raw is in NO cargo bench timed loop (symcontext_fork/_scaling only time fork(), and fork rebuilds dedup_set lazily so it's never cloned/populated there; assume_true/false use check_z3_dedup_if_seeded which never seeds); (2) within add_constraint_raw the dominant cost is the Z3 solver.assert + lineage scope work, not a usize-keyed lookup over tens of ptrs -- bottleneck is NOT the hash. Building a faithful isolating bench needs a bench-only pub reseed method (pollutes public API; benches are an external crate). CONCLUSION: std->FxHash swaps are now genuinely exhausted for cleanly-measurable wins; do NOT re-investigate dedup_set. See benchmark-memory-fxhash-stash-done (last real one) and offline-loop-queue-blocker-map.
avoid-mv-bak-revert-stale-cargo: Reverting an injected mutation with 'mv file.rs.bak file.rs' can leave cargo with a STALE build: mv preserves the .bak's mtime, which is older than the compiled artifact, so cargo declares the crate fresh and silently keeps running the mutant binary. Symptom: a test keeps failing (or passing) 'deterministically' after you believe you reverted, and the behaviour flips only once some unrelated source edit forces a real rebuild — reads exactly like a heisenbug. Cost one iteration chasing a phantom claripy_bridge Reverse-export bug (angr-sqfj8.19). Rule for mutation testing in this repo: restore by rewriting the file in place (python write / git checkout -- <path>), never 'mv .bak', and 'touch' the file after any restore. 'git checkout --' also updates mtime, so it is the safe default.
avoid-reset-solver-stats-in-tests: reset_solver_stats() must never be called from a Rust unit test. Six files delta-assert process-global stats counters inside measurement windows -- symbolic/context_tests/constraints.rs (plain after-before on ADD_CONSTRAINT_RAW_DEDUP_HIT_COUNT, underflows), syscalls/fd_io_tests.rs (symfile_reads_native, plain subtraction), memory/tests/symbolic_counters.rs (split out of the former memory/tests/symbolic.rs in angr-c7xno.56), memory/tests/ite_dedup.rs, symbolic/context_tests/solver_queries.rs, symbolic/context_tests/lineage.rs (post>pre style, fails rather than underflows) -- so no lock short of a crate-wide one makes a reset call safe under the parallel runner. Cover reset structurally instead: stats.rs's counter TABLES are looped over by BOTH get_solver_stats() (insert_counter_stats) and reset_solver_stats() (reset_counter_stats), which makes 'emitted but never cleared' unrepresentable, and each loop is unit-tested against local atomics. Since angr-03vl4.64 there are three tables, all with that treatment: CORE_COUNTERS (the standing engine counters, AtomicU64), WATERMARK_COUNTERS (AtomicU32 high-water marks, widened by the private ProfilingCounter trait), and MEASUREMENT_COUNTERS (the audit-scoped angr-g7nq/acoq/1joc groups). The helper pair was named insert_measurement_stats/reset_measurement_counters before that bead. Pair the tables with a key-list assertion (test_measurement_counter_keys_are_stable) -- mutation-verified as the only test that catches a typo'd key string, since the marker-bump wiring tests read keys from the same table. SIMPLIFY_SAMPLE_TICKER is the one counter deliberately outside every table (reset-but-never-emitted).
avoid-silent-no-op-callback-fallbacks: AVOID silent no-op fallbacks in PythonCallbacks *dispatch* call_* methods (e.g., the removed call_memory_store_symbolic_ast in callbacks/dispatch.rs returned Ok(()) doing nothing when its hook was unset). They mask wiring bugs: the engine appears to run but stores are silently dropped, leading to divergent memory between Rust and Python. Prefer hard errors that surface 'no such callback' to debugging silent corruption. Pattern (angr-12jjk.19, 2026-08-07): bind the slot with require_callback!(self.<slot>) -- a macro_rules in callbacks/mod.rs, pub(crate) use'd so submodules get it via 'use super::*'. It expands to the as_ref().ok_or_else(PyRuntimeError::new_err(...))? idiom the nine hard-erroring slots used to hand-write, and derives the '<slot> callback not set' message from the field ident via concat!(stringify!($field), ..) so slot/message drift is unexpressible. Exemplar: PythonCallbacks::call_lift_block. The enforcement site is dispatch_tests::unset_dispatch_callbacks_hard_error; add a probe there for any new dispatch callback. Two documented non-users: call_memory_store_symbolic_value (real degraded path -- concrete data falls back to a byte-level store, so its 'if let Some' stays to keep the fallback visible at the site) and the call_inspect_* family below. SCOPE (angr-9ke6b.20, 2026-08-03): the rule is NOT universal over call_*. The 18 call_inspect_* methods in callbacks/inspect.rs, all routed through PythonCallbacks::with_inspect_cb, intentionally return the 'absent' value (Ok(())/Ok(None)) for an unset slot -- state.inspect breakpoints are optional by design and are separately gated on inspect_event_enabled(N). That carve-out is spelled out in invariant 1 of the callbacks/mod.rs module docs; do not extend it to any callback the engine's correctness depends on. NOTE (angr-9ke6b.18, 2026-08-01): the old exemplar in this memory and in the callbacks/mod.rs module docs was call_on_hook, which was DEAD -- no Rust caller and no Python registration -- and has been deleted along with call_on_syscall and the CallbackSite::{OnHook,OnSyscall} profiling variants. Pick exemplars that production actually exercises; a dead exemplar cannot regress-test the invariant it advertises.
avoid-split-import-edit-ruff-autofix: GOTCHA (edit-hook autofix): the PostToolUse ruff hook (ruff --fix / ruff-format) runs after EVERY Edit. If you add an import in one Edit and its first USAGE in a LATER Edit, ruff's F401 unused-import autofix DELETES the import between the two edits (it was momentarily unused), leaving F821 'Undefined name' / NameError at runtime. Fix: add the import and at least one usage in the SAME edit, or re-add the import after writing the usages. Hit three independent times: adding 'from unittest import mock' to test_plugins.py (angr-szg45.1), consolidating RustFactoryPatch into tests/engines/conftest.py (angr-k8pc), and adding 'import contextlib' during the angr-ge7l SIM105 cleanup (try/except/pass -> contextlib.suppress).
avoid-stale-round2-audit-bead-premises: Round-2 audit epics angr-sqfj8 and angr-12jjk OVERLAP and their beads rot fast: five consecutive ralph iterations (120-124) claimed a bead whose premise was already fixed or duplicated (.55, .54, .51, .48). angr-sqfj8.48 (DRY the LengthLimiter/LoopBound eviction arms) was landed verbatim by angr-12jjk.20 the same week. RULE: before editing for any angr-sqfj8/angr-12jjk bead, open the cited site and re-verify the premise; if already fixed, 'git log -S<symbol> -- <file>' finds the fixing commit, then close with a bd note naming the canonical bead rather than the code change. Both epics are containers -- descend to leaves, never claim the epic row.
avoid-trusting-9ke6b-bead-citations: The .9ke6b audit children were filed 2026-07-31 against a pre-e2da4c1fa tree and their code citations have measurably rotted — verify before trusting. Concrete iter149 case: angr-9ke6b.201 cited 'cfg_fast.py:1454-1457: idx = search(...) then self._seg_list[idx]' as SegmentList::search's live consumer; that site is now _nodecode_bytes_ratio using iter_backward_from, and search() has zero in-tree callers outside segmentlist_tests.rs (filed as angr-9ke6b.232). Practice: grep for the cited symbol before writing a doc/comment that repeats the bead's caller claim, or you bake a stale citation into the source — exactly the class tools/check_line_citations.py exists to stop.
avoid-update-baseline-without-verificati: Running run_regression.py --full --update writes a single run's measurements as the new baseline. For Z3-nondeterministic benchmarks (rust_only=True), a single fast measurement bakes in a too-tight baseline that future noisy runs trip with false-positive regressions. Workflow: --update first, then run 3-5 verification rounds and bump any flagged entries above their slow-mode value. Confirmed 2026-05-09 on angr-6a7u: --update set google2016_unbreakable_1=1.683 (off a fast run) but max observed across 8 runs was 3.26 -- bumped to 3.5. RECONFIRMED 2026-07-16 (commit f804ba410): defcon2016quals_baby-re baseline was refreshed 0.53->0.33 by the libvex-ffi flip (807bfd74d) --update, but reproducible steady-state is 0.40-0.42s over 6 runs -> phantom 23% gate regression that survived --retry-failures. No code regression (bisect: reverting fork perf f5824dadc left it unchanged; only Python explore()/reporting edits landed since). Loosened to 0.42. Lesson: a fast bench (<0.5s) refreshed by a single --update run is especially prone to this; verify with 6 runs before trusting the --update value. MECHANIZED 2026-08-09 (angr-x6t9o): the 'bump any flagged entries above their slow-mode value' half of this workflow is now enforced by run_regression.py::PINNED_RUST_TIMES, which --update honors — see avoid-update-clobbering-pinned-baselines. Put a verified pessimistic value in that table rather than only in the JSON, or the next blanket --update reverts your verification.
avoid-update-clobbering-pinned-baselines: run_regression.py --update writes one run's measurement over EVERY baseline, including ones deliberately pinned to a bench's slow/pessimistic mode. cow_fork_scaling's pin was documented only in a REGRESSION_SUITE comment and got demoted twice by blanket refreshes (807bfd74d -> 2.559, dbad6440c -> 2.5) with no warning, reddening the ralph gate for a dozen iterations (angr-x6t9o). Pins now live in run_regression.py::PINNED_RUST_TIMES and --update honors them, printing a 'pinned baseline kept:' line with the measurement it declined to write; apply_pinned_baselines() treats a pin as floor AND ceiling so a slow read cannot ratchet the gate looser either. RULE: a pin belongs in that table, never only in a comment — a comment does not survive --update. Diagnostic that separates this from host noise: compare in-gate reads to standalone run_single.py reads of the same commit. cow_fork_scaling read 2.87-3.14s in-gate vs 2.45-2.51s standalone because the ralph gate runs right after 'cargo test --release' in a loaded 6G scope and it is the most memory-heavy fast-tier bench (1051 MB peak vs 393 MB next); angr-mc8pw's suite-median normalization does NOT cover that, since the sub-second benches are fixed-startup-dominated and drag the median to ~0.98 while every multi-second bench runs ~1.15x slow.
avoid-vacuous-offload-test-serde-budget: Scheduler serde-budget gate makes offload tests pass VACUOUSLY: any Rust unit test that calls exploration::scheduler_worker::offload_surplus MORE THAN ONCE over the same SchedulerCounters must preset counters.step_ns (e.g. u64::MAX/8). The first call's detach_timed charges serde_ns, and offload_is_affordable is serde*SERDE_BUDGET_DIVISOR <= step — with the default step_ns==0 the budget shuts Trigger A off for every later call, so the test asserts 'nothing was offloaded' for the wrong reason. Caught by mutation-check during angr-fs8kb.5 (test_trigger_a_nets_out_states_already_queued_for_idle_siblings): the pre-fix semantics PASSED the test until step_ns was preset. Corollary of the general rule — always mutation-check a scheduler test, because the budget gate is a second, invisible reason for a zero-offload outcome.
